a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: Multiple human oral-bioavailability records for polar carboxylic-acid/amide drugs with cyclohexane or cyclic-urea motifs report F values above the 20% threshold: tranexamic acid 33.4% (C21), gabapentin 37.7% (C28), penicillin V 54.8% in normal children (C24), biotin ~100% (C09), captopril ~60% (C05), and alpha-lipoic acid ~25-30% (C03).

The query contains a carboxylic acid, secondary amide, barbiturate/cyclic-imide core, and two cyclohexyl groups; the lipophilic cyclohexyl/barbiturate portion can offset the polar ionized acid, and the closest structural contexts (cyclohexane carboxylic acids and acyl amino acids) all exceed F=20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule itself.
Transferability from polar acid/amide contexts is indirect; the query is more polar (logD -4.19) and larger than tranexamic acid or gabapentin.
Unknown whether the query is a substrate for intestinal transporters (e.g., PEPT1, OATP) or undergoes significant first-pass metabolism/efflux.
No formulation- or dose-specific data for the query.
content.decision_summary: Although the physicochemical prior is low, the available L1 records for structurally related polar carboxylic-acid/amide drugs (tranexamic acid, gabapentin, penicillin V, biotin, captopril, alpha-lipoic acid) all show human oral bioavailability above 20%. The query's cyclohexyl/barbiturate lipophilic core and carboxylic acid/amide polar groups align with these contexts, so F >= 20% is better supported than F < 20%.
